title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 8
summary: Brent oil approached $100 a barrel, before paring some of its gains, after Saudi Arabia said operations at several energy facilities in the kingdom’s south were halted by attacks.

summary: Wheat climbed as Russia rejected a proposed moratorium on attacks against ships carrying civilian goods in the Black Sea, heightening concerns about prolonged disruptions to grain shipments in the vital trade corridor.

title: Stocks Slide as Oil Rally Fuels Inflation Jitters: Markets Wrap

title: Singapore Air Defended by Government on Air India, Expansion
summary: The Singapore government is backing Singapore Airlines investment in foreign carriers, including its financial support for loss-making Air India, as the company seeks to strengthen its position abroad.

title: Stock Resiliency Depends on Moves by the Fed, Says Principal’s Shah
summary: “The next couple of months are likely to be pretty rocky with only modest gains to be had for the rest of the year,” says Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management. Shah says a possible series of hikes by the Federal Reserve can provide some resistance for equities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Attacks Halt Saudi Energy Sites, Novartis Drops Most in 6 Years | The Opening Trade 9/8/2026
summary:
Brent oil surged toward $100 a barrel after Saudi Arabia halted some energy operations near its border with Yemen due to attacks, highlighting risks to supply from the region.

Novartis shares plunge as much as 10%, marking the worst day since 2020, after its del-desiran treatment for a rare muscle-wasting disease failed to meet the primary endpoint in a phase 3 trial. Vontobel said this is another “major pipeline setback.”

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: Rate hikes, elections, fiscal concerns threaten to upend markets.

title: Novartis Sees Avidity Drug Suffer Third Clinical-Trial Setback
summary: Novartis saw a treatment for a rare muscle-wasting disease fail a late-stage study, the third clinical-trial setback in a week. The medicine was the centerpiece of Novartis’s $12 billion takeover of Avidity Biosciences and raises questions about the drugmaker’s growth prospects. Fabienne Kinzelmann reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cowan: South Africa Has Yet to Turn Growth Corner
summary: David Cowan, Africa Economist at Citi Research, says South Africa has yet to turn the corner on growth, with the economy showing resilience rather than a strong acceleration. He also says Zimbabwe’s recovery is benefiting from improved fiscal discipline, higher gold and lithium prices and stronger agricultural exports.  Cowan discusses the challenges of de-dollarization, signs of renewed foreign investor interest and the importance of Zimbabwe getting its lithium policy right with Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Global Bond Rush Builds With Issuers Racing to Avoid Headwinds
summary: Borrowers around the globe are rushing to debt markets on Tuesday, kicking off what is likely to be one of the busiest sessions of the year for bond markets.

title: UniCredit Buys Stake in German Fintech in Digital Markets Push
summary: UniCredit SpA has acquired a minority stake in German lending markets platform VC Trade as the Italian bank seeks to expand its digital capital markets capabilities in debt transactions.

title: Old Mutual Wants South Africa’s Newest Bank Profitable by 2028
summary: Profit at Old Mutual declined for the first time since 2022 as risk-off sentiment from conflicts in the Middle East curbed investment returns at the Africa’s biggest insurer by assets.
